title: 第3章 剑尘长老第4章 试炼之门
content_zh:
顾渊是被敲门声吵醒的。
不是门，是窗户。
有人在用指节轻轻叩击木窗框，三短一长，像是某种约定好的暗号。
顾渊睁开眼。
天已经黑了，屋里没有点灯，只有从窗纸缝隙里漏进来的一点微弱月光，在泥地上切出一道苍白的细线。
他睡了整整一下午。
窗框又被叩响。
三短一长。
顾渊撑着身体坐起来，稻草床板发出熟悉的吱呀声。
他走到窗边，推开一条缝。
朱八斗那张硕大的圆脸挤在窗缝里，眯着眼睛往里瞅。
“醒了？“胖厨子的声音压得很低，像是怕惊动什么。
顾渊点点头。
“门边的食盒看见没有？“
顾渊转头看向门边。
黑暗中，一个方形的轮廓静静躺在那里，隐约还能闻到一丝肉香。
“看见了。“
“吃了。“
“……嗯。“
朱八斗似乎满意了，咂了咂嘴：“明天寅时，食堂后门，我给你留热的。别让我等。“

说完，他的圆脸从窗缝里消失，脚步声渐渐远去，很快就被夜风吹散了。
顾渊站在窗边，沉默了很久。
夜风从窗缝灌进来，带着深秋的凉意。
他关上窗，走到门边，摸到那个食盒。
盒子还有余温，里面的米粥已经凉了，但两个肉包子用布包着，尚有些热气。
顾渊坐在稻草床上，一个一个地吃完。
他吃得很慢，每一口都嚼很久。
不是因为食物珍贵，而是他在想事情。
想什么，他自己也说不清楚。
只是有一种很奇怪的感觉——像是常年干涸的河床上，忽然渗出了一小股水。
不多，不足以解渴，但确实湿润了一小块泥土。
吃完，他将食盒放到门边，重新躺下。
这一次，他做了一个梦。
梦里他站在一片无边无际的荒原上，手里握着剑，面前是一座高得看不见顶的山。
他一直在挥剑，一剑又一剑，山纹丝不动。
但他没有停，因为他知道，总有一天，山会塌的。
天还没亮，顾渊就醒了。
这一次不是疼醒的。
是饿醒的——昨天那顿晚饭和今天这顿早饭之间的间隔太短，胃被唤醒了，开始抗议。
他起身，用冷水抹了把脸，系好草鞋，提着剑推开门。

雾气比昨天更浓了。
content_en:
Gu Yuan was woken up by the knock on the door.
Not a door, but a window.
Someone is tapping the wooden window frame lightly with his knuckles, three short and one long, like some agreed-upon code.
Gu Yuan opened his eyes.
It was already dark, and there were no lights in the room. There was only a faint moonlight leaking in through the cracks in the window paper, cutting a pale thin line on the dirt.
He slept all afternoon.
The window frame was knocked again.
Three short and one long.
Gu Yuan sat up with his body propped up, and the straw bed board made a familiar creaking sound.
He walked to the window and opened it a crack.
Zhu Badou's huge round face was squeezed into the crack of the window, squinting and looking in.
"Are you awake?" The fat cook's voice was very low, as if he was afraid of disturbing anything.
Gu Yuan nodded.
"Did you see the food box by the door?"
Gu Yuan turned to look at the door.
In the darkness, a square silhouette lay there quietly, and there was a faint smell of meat.
"Saw it."
"Eat."
"...Hmm."
Zhu Badou seemed satisfied and smacked his lips: "At Yin time tomorrow, I will leave something hot for you at the back door of the cafeteria. Don't make me wait."
After saying that, his round face disappeared from the crack of the window, and the sound of footsteps gradually faded away, and was soon blown away by the night wind.
Gu Yuan stood by the window and was silent for a long time.
The night breeze came in through the cracks in the window, bringing with it the coolness of late autumn.
He closed the window, walked to the door, and touched the food box.
The box was still warm, and the rice porridge inside had gone cold, but the two meat buns were wrapped in cloth and were still warm.
Gu Yuan sat on the straw bed and finished eating one by one.
He ate slowly, chewing each bite for a long time.
Not because the food is precious, but because he is thinking about something.
He couldn't tell what he was thinking.
There was just a very strange feeling - like a small stream of water suddenly seeping out of the river bed that had been dry all year round.
Not much, not enough to quench your thirst, but it did moisten a small patch of dirt.
After eating, he put the food box next to the door and lay down again.
This time, he had a dream.
In the dream, he stood on an endless wasteland, holding a sword in his hand. In front of him was a mountain so high that the top could not be seen.
He kept swinging his sword, one sword after another, and the mountain didn't move at all.
But he didn't stop, because he knew that one day, the mountain would collapse.
Gu Yuan woke up before dawn.
This time it wasn't pain that woke me up.
I woke up from hunger - the gap between yesterday's dinner and today's breakfast was too short, my stomach was awakened and started to protest.
He stood up, wiped his face with cold water, tied up his straw sandals, and opened the door with his sword.
The fog is thicker than yesterday.
